replication.target_description: Study 1 animal-meat reminder versus meat-alone images: animal empathy or willingness to eat meat; exact assigned outcome/test unresolved.

notes: Identity verified from repository cover: Earle, Megan, Hodson, Gordon, Dhont, Kristof and MacInnis, Cara C. (2019), matching title Eating with our eyes (closed): Effects of visually associating animals with meat on anti-vegan/vegetarian attitudes and meat consumption willingness, journal 22(6), pp. 818–835, and version-of-record DOI 10.1177/1368430219861848. Document explicitly identified as Author’s Accepted Manuscript; canonical text contains manuscript pages 1–40 including methods, results, tables, discussion and references. No PDF supplied. Locator p. 6 cannot be equated directly to accepted-manuscript p. 6 (background); relevant Study 1 results are manuscript pp. 12–17. Both rows have identical Study 1 descriptions naming empathy AND willingness to eat meat in relation to the animal-image manipulation, without an outcome-specific/test-specific identifier. Table 1 prints manipulation–animal empathy r = .43, p < .001, and manipulation–willingness to eat meat r = -.31, p < .001. These are distinct candidates; neither can be assigned to either audit_id from the supplied locator. Table 1 codes reminder +1 and control –1. No conversion or row-order assignment performed. Common Study 1 sample candidate: 299 participants after exclusions (duplicate IP addresses 3, non-meat-eaters 13, attention-check failures 38); Results specifies FIML for missing data. Footnote 3 says those unwilling to eat particular meats were retained, contrary to preregistration. Since row-specific test correspondence remains unresolved, N is retained only as a candidate for parent field-scope review, not asserted as target analytic N. No N derived from df or recruitment total. Original side and reported_success are unassigned placeholders, not findings about availability or author verdict.
